correctness.rationale: The ten geometric lines give the connected cubic Kneser graph on two-subsets of five labels; transverse pair intersections with no triangles give ordinary nodes, three on each rational component, hence stability and genus six. The normalization gluing torus has character lattice the integral signed cycle kernel, not unsigned edges or the critical group. An independent incidence-matrix construction recovered a basis with identity chord coordinates via the tree minor and verified every frozen 6-by-6 change of basis by exact GU=UB and determinant ±1. Positive cyclic blocks yield Weil restrictions, a negative length-one block yields N₂, and a negative length-two block gives the restricted quadratic norm-one factor Q₄. Finite field multiplicative groups and their norm kernels are cyclic, giving the asserted products uniformly in q, including characteristic two. Direct orbit counts reproduced the full catalog: (2²,1) has two fixed nodes with swapped branches and (4,1) has one. A point outside the node set lifts uniquely to the normalization, so the precise correction is fixed nodes minus fixed branches. A fixed normalized component has q^n+1 points; the surface has only the point, volume, and Picard trace terms, since its Picard module is the permutation representation on the five conic classes (over Q_l the classes form a basis). Subtracting gives the complement count; log-generating the fixed-point orbit counts gives the stated products. The point-count proof is via normalization, not an empirical claim from the sample q tests.
